name: Shelly Lazarus
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Lazarus joined Ogilvy & Mather as an entry-level account executive in 1971 (age 24) and held no senior role until becoming President of O&M Direct in 1989 (age 42); she became CEO in 1996 (age 49).
early_history_summary: Lazarus grew up in Brooklyn, graduated from Smith College in 1968, and earned an MBA from Columbia in 1970. She briefly worked at Clairol as an assistant product manager before joining Ogilvy & Mather as an account executive in 1971, a standard entry-level advertising role.
family_context_summary: Born in Brooklyn to Lewis Braff, a certified public accountant, and Sylvia Braff. Middle-class family; father was a CPA.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family background in advertising or marketing.
evidence_summary: Lazarus rose through Ogilvy & Mather over decades, becoming CEO at age 49 in 1996. Her early career consisted of standard entry-level advertising roles (account executive from 1971) with no material milestone by age 26. She attended Smith College and Columbia Business School, both selective institutions, but her defining achievements came in her 40s and 50s.

name: Indra Nooyi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Nooyi earned her Yale master's degree in 1980 (age 24) and began as a consultant at the Boston Consulting Group; her first executive role came at Motorola in 1986 (age 31), and she joined PepsiCo in 1994 (age 39), becoming CEO in 2006 (age 51).
early_history_summary: Nooyi grew up in Chennai (then Madras), India, and earned bachelor's degrees from the University of Madras in 1975 and a postgraduate diploma from IIM Calcutta in 1976. She moved to the U.S. in 1978 to attend Yale School of Management, graduating in 1980 before starting as a BCG consultant.
family_context_summary: Born in Madras (Chennai), India; father worked at the State Bank of Hyderabad, mother was a homemaker. Middle-class Indian family; mother encouraged strategic thinking through dinner-table exercises.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family background in business or corporate strategy.
evidence_summary: Nooyi's path to prominence was a long corporate climb: Yale MBA (1980), six years at BCG, executive roles at Motorola and ABB, then PepsiCo SVP in 1994 at age 39. She became CEO of PepsiCo in 2006 at age 51. By age 26 she had only just begun her consulting career at BCG with no material milestone.
